target_customer: Mortgage lenders and brokers, including non-agency, VA, FHA and subprime lenders, who need borrower documents and data
problem: Loan officers spend about a third of their time asking borrowers for documents that exist online; Lendsnap pulled original statements by linking to borrower financial accounts.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to lenders and mortgage brokers (pricing not found)
product_category: Mortgage technology, document and data collection

founders.name: Orion Parrott
education: MBA, UC Berkeley (per a GrowthMentor article that spells his name Orion Willow and Orian in the body)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Founder/Founding CEO; YC blog (August 2016) says he grew up watching his father build a real estate portfolio and has invested in real estate for about twenty years. The name Orion Willow in the GrowthMentor article is assumed to be the same person but is not confirmed.

founders.name: Mike Romano
previous_startups: YC-backed mortgage technology startup (named as Lendsnap by inference only; the YC page does not name it)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder and VP of Business Development, now at Stairs Financial. Kingscrowd (via search) says Parrott and Romano founded the company in August 2014.

exit.reason: Not stated by the company. An investor-focused account says it could not convince enough lenders to use its technology; one source says the shutdown was in 2019. Both are weak.

competitors.name: Blend
competitors.what: Mortgage technology company building digital borrower experiences and document collection for lenders
competitors.funding_then: $40M Series C announced in January 2016 led by Founders Fund

competitors.name: Quicken Loans
competitors.what: Large lender that the YC launch post says was starting to adopt account-linking for mortgage documents
competitors.traction_then: Largest US retail lender at the time (per general context, not the post)

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed aggregation of original statements from hundreds of institutions, payroll and tax sites, secure data handling and lender workflow integration; hard but based on existing account-linking technology.

defensibility.rationale: Account-linking relationships and lender integrations help, but the YC post notes incumbents were adopting similar approaches and the company claimed to be the only one delivering original electronic statements, which was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded rivals such as Blend kept building borrower portals and document collection, and the account-linking infrastructure was being commoditized.

market_need_then: The company claimed lenders would write $1.5T of mortgages in 2017 and spend $15B on human labor evaluating borrowers, and the YC post says its process takes under 30 minutes and lifts loan officer productivity 30 to 50%. These are company claims, not independent data.

branding.domain_note: Listed website now redirects to openfpga.ai, which redirects to an unrelated site (isochron.cloud).

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline 'The Digital Mortgage Company'; claims to be easy and safe for borrowers.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand and constant confusion with LoanSnap, a different mortgage company that raised about $100M, and with Snapdocs.

outcome_analysis: Lendsnap was a Summer 2016 company that gathered original borrower documents for mortgage lenders and raised little disclosed money, a 2017 convertible note on a crowdfunding listing. A weak investor-focused account says it could not convince enough lenders, and one source dates its end to 2019, but no company post-mortem exists. Because the cause is not confirmed by a reliable source, failure factors are left empty although Blend and big lenders competed in the same space.
notes: The 2017-08-08 convertible note rests on a single outlet (Kingscrowd, seen only through search results as the page returned HTTP 403). The snippet says $6M valuation and $1.38M total raised; the $6M is not recorded as post-money because it is a note valuation and the $1.38M is a total, not this round's amount. Crunchbase shows a seed with no amount. Shutdown year 2019 and the cause rest on weak aggregator text (persana.ai, CB Insights status). Headquarters conflict (San Francisco, Berkeley, Oakland). Do not confuse with LoanSnap. YC lists no outcome analysis. The YC page lists the website as openfpga.ai, which redirects elsewhere, so the company site is dead.
